activity_summary: Mistress Ansell asked if this was the king who was dying or a new trouble. You said the dying was the second act, and that he has come ashore in Wales and puts his hand to the earth. She hoped the ground is not the point, and she did not say who takes the crown. You said you wrote a little more this morning and are done until the speech. The loaf was a penny and a finger and a half short. Board was threepence because you sat. You did not ask who puts him down. She did not offer that verdict.

entities.name: Mistress Dorcas Ansell
entities.context: Asked with the jug in her hand, and hoped the ground was not the point.

entities.name: Alse Pinder
entities.context: Named the threepence, and left the three words alone.

entities.name: Gillis Verbeke
entities.context: Took the greeting as not a grave, and kept his name off the act.

entities.name: William Shakespeare
entities.context: Said he is ashore, refused the larger verdict, and sat.

entities.name: Richard II
entities.context: Mentioned in The ground is not the point
